claims.claim: Mousnier-Lompré says he makes a point of Frenchifying the names Hobb invents, whether proper nouns or common nouns.
claims.source: Arnaud Mousnier-Lompré, interviewed by dwalan, Elbakin.net exclusive interview, 2 February 2010
claims.quote: je m'efforce de franciser les noms que Robin invente

claims.claim: Mousnier-Lompré grounds his naming policy on the premise that the world Hobb describes does not exist.
claims.source: Arnaud Mousnier-Lompré, interviewed by dwalan, Elbakin.net exclusive interview, 2 February 2010
claims.quote: le monde qu'elle décrit n'existe pas

claims.claim: Mousnier-Lompré judged the literal French rendering of Hobb's 'hunting cat' as 'chat de chasse' not pretty, and coined 'marguet' instead.
claims.source: Arnaud Mousnier-Lompré, interviewed by dwalan, Elbakin.net exclusive interview, 2 February 2010

claims.claim: Before naming Hobb's 'hunting cat' Mousnier-Lompré first asked Hobb how she pictured the animal.
claims.source: Arnaud Mousnier-Lompré, interviewed by dwalan, Elbakin.net exclusive interview, 2 February 2010
claims.quote: j'ai demandé d'abord à Robin comment elle imaginait le bestiau

claims.claim: Mousnier-Lompré says he tries to render in French the overtones a Hobb name evokes for an English-speaking reader, turning 'colonel Haren' into 'Lièvrin'.
claims.source: Arnaud Mousnier-Lompré, interviewed by dwalan, Elbakin.net exclusive interview, 2 February 2010
claims.quote: je tâche de rendre en français les harmoniques que ce nom évoque

claims.claim: Mousnier-Lompré says Hobb writes very well and very clearly, in a settled, considered style.
claims.source: Arnaud Mousnier-Lompré, interviewed by dwalan, Elbakin.net exclusive interview, 2 February 2010
claims.quote: très bien, très clairement, avec un style posé, réfléchi
claims.page: answer on whether her writing has changed

claims.claim: Mousnier-Lompré says translating is not knowing the source language by heart but knowing the target language intimately.
claims.source: Arnaud Mousnier-Lompré, interviewed by Allan, Fantastinet, 28 March 2006
claims.quote: Traduire, ce n’est pas connaître la langue d’origine par coeur

claims.claim: Mousnier-Lompré says that where the sense matters crucially, as with Hobb, he contacts the author to discuss a particular turn of phrase.
